records.context: Runs the steps of this module in order. Divisions are read with :func:`division_events`; ``mode='auto'`` keeps whichever kind, fission or budding, the movie has more of. Each division is checked (parent seen at ``t_div`` and on 80% of the window, daughters seen on the next frame, two daughters for a fission). The kept divisions get size-matched controls (:func:`match_controls`) and a shuffled alignment (:func:`shuffled_alignment`) with its own size-matched controls, so the null runs the same matching at a random time. The late-vs-baseline change of every unit (:func:`unit_changes`) is compared as Hedges' g (:func:`effect_size`), dividing against control and shuffled against its control. Complete fission cycles give the size-control fits.

The alpha phenotype path adds ``"ph_flatfield"``, ``"ph_segment"``, ``"ph_measure"``, ``"ph_masks"``, ``"merge"`` and ``"aggregate"``, run only when named here and after those four; ``ph_flatfield`` builds the laboratory microplate's maps once, before the microplate sample positions, and ``ph_masks`` writes each cell's microscope field of view-edge flags and flat-microscope field of view gains from the saved masks. A run of only these needs ``dst_root`` and ``plate`` but no ``genotype_source``, takes its microplate sample positions from ``ops_phenotype``, and adds to each microplate sample position's ``ops_report.json`` rather than replacing it. ``aggregate`` pools the microplate sample positions run and writes ``ops_guides_<plate>`` and ``ops_genes_<plate>``.

records.source: any of ``"stitch"``, ``"phenotype"``, ``"objects"`` and ``"decode"``, run in that order. A phase left out reads what it needs from the database, so a well can be stitched once and decoded again. records.context: THE MAP. Per laboratory microplate and channel, a few hundred microscope fields of view are read, block-averaged in 16 x 16 pixel blocks, and the per-block median over the microscope fields of view is taken. Cells move from microscope field of view to microscope field of view while the illumination does not, so the median keeps the illumination and loses the cells. It is smoothed with a Gaussian (sigma 6 blocks, about 96 microscope field of view pixels); the nuclear channel, whose sparse bright nuclei leave a noisier median, is then fitted with a 4th-order 2-D polynomial. The camera and background offset ``b`` is the 0.1th percentile of every block mean, and the map is ``flat = (smooth - b) / (centre - b)``: 1 at the centre. It is floored at 0.25, so no pixel is multiplied by more than 4.

records.context: The Make Masks timelapse run writes one results folder per tracked field under ``tracks/division/`` when ``timelapse_division_analysis`` is on (see :func:`spacr.division_analysis.write_division_results`). This panel reads such a folder, or finds the result folders under any folder above them, and draws the three figures from its tables: the aligned trajectories of dividing cells against matched controls and the shuffled alignment, the forest plot of effect sizes, and the size-control plot. Nothing is recomputed; the tables on disk are what is drawn.
